clue.text: Part of spectacular Christmas tree

indicators.note: a part of something is a piece cut out of it, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

parts.note: the last letters of the first word run on into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A dazzling decorated tree at Christmas, or a bit of one.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'tree' defines; 'Christmas' lends its first two letters to the hidden run and dresses the surface. SpectacuLAR CHristmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The larch is a deciduous conifer, a kind of tree.

clue.text: Place of pilgrimage, terribly old? Sure

indicators.note: something done terribly is botched and messed up, so the letters are put in disorder

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pilgrimage site is very ancient and gets an emphatic yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lourdes in south-west France is a famous Catholic shrine visited by millions of pilgrims.

clue.text: Something to eat in bar, almost cooked

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub snack that is nearly done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' looks like a cue to drop a letter, but every letter of it is part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Roast lamb is a classic Sunday dish, so it is food.

clue.text: A woman may wear this hat touring Ireland — almost new

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go round it, so one word wraps around the others
almost means not quite all, so the word that follows loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written; it is the outer shell
taken as written
IR is a standard abbreviation for Ireland
taken as written, then cut short

explanation.surface: Fashion advice: a woman might sport this hat while travelling round Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'woman may wear this'; 'A' opens the surface as if part of it, but belongs to the wordplay. 'Hat' looks like the thing worn; it is only the outer shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairnet is a fine mesh worn over the hair to hold it in place, traditionally by women.

clue.text: Enraged at fancy open-air restaurant

indicators.note: fancy as a verb is to imagine, so the letters are freely reimagined in another order

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a pretentious outdoor eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea garden is an outdoor café where refreshments are served among lawns and flowers.

clue.text: Take an unnecessary risk in state capital, supporting draw

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting word holds up another from below, so it comes second

parts.note: to draw someone in is to entice or tempt them
Providence is the capital of Rhode Island

explanation.surface: Someone gambles needlessly on a stalemate in some state's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue one part 'supporting' another sits beneath it, so the capital goes below the word for draw.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt providence is an idiom for courting misfortune by acting rashly.

clue.text: Type of treatment, a type they knock inside

parts.note: a is taken as written; a version is a type or variant

indicators.note: inside says one piece is placed within the word before it

parts.note: taken as written; it is split around the next piece
to rap is to knock

explanation.surface: Puzzled description of a therapy: the kind where people bang about indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' appears twice on purpose: once in the definition, once as wordplay for a variant. 'Inside' applies only to the knock, which sits within the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion therapy is a psychological treatment pairing an unwanted habit with something unpleasant.

clue.text: Startle a teller, firstly, entering safe

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something entering goes into another word, so it sits within it

parts.note: sound means safe and secure, as in safe and sound

indicators.note: firstly points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: first letter of teller

explanation.surface: A robber surprises a bank teller by breaking into the safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safe' looks like the bank's strongbox; here it is the adjective, as in safe and sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound is to amaze or shock, a stronger synonym of startle.

clue.text: Director to study fear

parts.note: D is a standard abbreviation for director
to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A film director decides to research the theme of fear.
explanation.walkthrough: To read a subject is British usage for studying it at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is a deep, anxious fear of what may happen.

clue.text: Character smashed tea urn

indicators.note: something smashed is broken into bits, so its letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: A clumsy person breaks the tea urn.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's nature is their temperament or basic character.

clue.text: Metal in skull? Head's not the same

indicators.note: the first letter is no longer what it was, so the opening letter is swapped for another

parts.note: the cranium is the skull

explanation.surface: A metal plate fitted in someone's skull leaves them never quite the same.
explanation.walkthrough: CRANIUM changes its first letter, C becoming U. The clue does not say which letter goes in; the definition and crossings decide.
explanation.definitionFit: Uranium is a heavy radioactive metallic element used as nuclear fuel.

clue.text: Ask earnestly to go in and dine, being short of energy

indicators.note: being short of something means lacking it, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: to go in is to enter
to dine is to eat
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Pleading with someone to come in and eat while running low on energy.
explanation.walkthrough: ENTER and EAT join, then one E (the second in ENTER) is dropped to give ENTREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or implore someone seriously.

clue.text: Blows up, having frightful set-to with dean

indicators.note: frightful means awful and chaotic, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, hyphen dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper after a terrible argument with the college dean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blows up' is the explosive sense, not losing one's temper. A set-to is a fight or quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Detonates means explodes, as a bomb does when set off.

clue.text: Ready to go down, with reservations, to eat first course

parts.note: under means down, below
requests to eat the first course of a meal, read as orders for the dish served first

explanation.surface: A diner booked in at a restaurant, ready to sit down and order the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: A starter is the British name for a first course, so orders for it are a starter's orders. In horse racing the phrase means the horses are lined up and awaiting the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Under starter's orders is the racing idiom for runners poised and ready to begin.

clue.text: See 12
Counting, or estimating?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: adding up or calculating a total
second meaning: judging or supposing roughly

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints that both words are the same verb in different senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is both to calculate a figure and, colloquially, to think or guess, so both participles fit.

clue.text: Overcoats in bar, unrestricted part of train

indicators.note: unrestricted letters are free to roam, so they settle into a new order

parts.note: all three words taken as written

explanation.surface: Coats hung in a pub, with drinking going on freely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but its letters belong to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: An observation car is a railway carriage with large windows for viewing the scenery.

clue.text: Speak non-stop

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to put into words
second meaning: an adjective for a fast train or service with no stops

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an order to talk without pausing; really it is two unrelated senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a thought is to voice it, and an express train runs through without stopping.

clue.text: Work in musical drama, note

parts.note: an opera is a drama set to music
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A singer's job in an opera, perhaps hitting one note.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or run, as a machine works.

clue.text: Sappers reportedly go free

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the spoken form is what counts

parts.note: to go is to leave; the spelling changes but the sound stays

explanation.surface: Army engineers are said to be released from duty.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps whose soldiers are sappers. RE plus a word sounding like 'leave' gives RELIEVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone of a burden is to free them from it.

clue.text: High value head of expedition placed on climbing experiences

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of expedition

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to meet with something is to experience it

explanation.surface: A mountaineering party's leader prizes the experiences of climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Placed on' in a down clue puts the E on top of the reversed word. 'Climbing' looks like the expedition's activity.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteem is high regard, the value placed on someone.

clue.text: Scallywag affected by school, at first

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word just before it

parts.note: first letter of school
camp means affected, theatrically exaggerated

explanation.surface: A young rascal has been shaped by school from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Affected' looks like 'influenced'; here it means mannered and showy.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a mischievous rascal, especially a child, just as a scallywag is.

clue.text: Runs in a boy responsible for fire-raising

indicators.note: in places one piece within the words that follow it

parts.note: a is taken as written; a boy is a son
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A boy dashes about after starting a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property, called fire-raising in Scots law.

clue.text: Fuel that is stored in dollies abroad

indicators.note: something stored in another thing sits inside it
abroad means all over the place, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Fuel kept in trolleys overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel oil is the heavy petroleum fuel burnt in diesel engines.

clue.text: Oriental festival's name

parts.note: Easter is a Christian festival; the 's means 'has'
N is a standard abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Asking what an Eastern festival is called.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'has': the festival is followed by N.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriental and eastern both describe things from Asia or the East.

clue.text: A sin to devour a third of tiramisu — this one?

indicators.note: to devour something is to swallow it, so one word takes in another

parts.note: taken as written
a vice is a sin or moral failing
taken as written

indicators.note: a third of a word here means its third letter

parts.note: third letter of tiramisu

explanation.surface: Gobbling a chunk of tiramisu: which of the deadly sins is that?
explanation.walkthrough: 'A third of tiramisu' looks like a portion of the dessert; it is the word a plus the dessert's third letter. 'This one' means the sin the clue is about; gluttony is the false path, and the wordplay rules it out.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice, greed for wealth, is one of the seven deadly sins, so it is a sin of the kind named.

clue.text: Comprehensive knowledge about working in a religious community

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round another

parts.note: mastery of a subject is thorough knowledge of it
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone with deep learning working in a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: A monastery is the community of monks living together under religious vows, or their building.

clue.text: Slip lead off dog fetching bird

indicators.note: slipping a lead off removes the front, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound

explanation.surface: A dog walker unclips the leash and the dog brings back a bird it caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'lead' is a dog's leash in the surface, but here it means the leading letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The eagle is a large bird of prey.
